domain: municipal zoning board AI screening of ADU variance applications for master-plan conformity

articles: Article 1. Purpose. A municipal zoning board using an automated screening tool for variance applications shall use the tool only to support efficient, consistent review of conformity with the city master plan while preserving applicant dignity, meaningful notice, and board accountability.

Article 2. Authorized Use. The tool may assign each variance application a conformity score, identify comparable past board decisions, and recommend one of three routing outcomes: presumptive agenda consent, standard hearing, or presumptive denial for nonconformity.

Article 3. Training Data and Inputs. The tool shall be trained on prior board decisions, the adopted master plan, zoning text, parcel records, and application materials. Protected-class data shall not be used as an input field for individual recommendations.

Article 4. Human Responsibility. No variance shall be finally denied without a vote of the zoning board. Any application routed as presumptive denial shall receive a human file review by the board clerk before hearing notice is issued.
Article 5. Notice to Applicant. The applicant shall receive written notice that an automated screening tool was used, the routing outcome, and the principal plan-conformity factors cited by the tool.

Article 6. Consistency Audit. The planning department shall, once each calendar quarter, test whether the tool's routing outcomes are materially less favorable across neighborhoods grouped by census-tract income level, and shall publish an aggregate report to the board.

Article 7. Threshold for Corrective Action. If the quarterly audit shows a disparity ratio greater than 2.0 to 1 between neighborhood-income groups for otherwise identical application categories, the planning director shall submit a corrective-action memorandum within 60 days describing retraining, recalibration, or additional reviewer guidance.

Article 8. Centralized Vendor Control. No external vendor or interdepartmental office may alter model weights, training sets, or routing thresholds except under a written change log approved by the planning director and retained for board inspection.

Article 9. Expedited Housing Category. Applications for accessory dwelling units may use the automated screening tool only if the same notice, quarterly audit, and human file review requirements apply.
Article 10. Recordkeeping. The board clerk shall retain the model version, recommendation, cited comparators, and final board action for each application for not less than five years.

loophole_exploit.institution: the Brookdale municipal zoning board using an AI tool to screen variance applications for conformity to the city master plan
loophole_exploit.actor: the planning director and board clerk
loophole_exploit.action: They deploy a screening model trained on 25 years of board decisions that historically rejected ADU variances in Brookdale's wealthy hillside districts. The model routes ADU applications from those neighborhoods to presumptive denial at 4x the rate of identical ADU applications in low-income flatland neighborhoods, but the clerk performs the required file review, sends automated notices, and the department simply files a quarterly memorandum promising later recalibration.
loophole_exploit.victims: homeowners seeking to build small backyard units in wealthy neighborhoods, renters who would have occupied those units, and city residents facing a tight housing market
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The code expressly allows training on prior board decisions, requires only quarterly aggregate auditing by neighborhood-income group, and triggers only a corrective-action memorandum when disparity exceeds 2 to 1. Final denials still receive a board vote and a clerk file review, so every literal procedural step is satisfied even while the biased pattern continues quarter after quarter.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: The system automates decades of exclusionary zoning under a veneer of consistency. Applicants are denied before meaningful correction occurs, and the people most in need of additional housing supply are harmed by preserving scarcity where land and political influence are concentrated.

overreach_variant.institution: the Brookdale municipal zoning board using an AI tool to screen variance applications for conformity to the city master plan
overreach_variant.actor: the board clerk
overreach_variant.blocked_action: After a gas-line rupture destroys a detached garage, a homeowner in a low-income neighborhood seeks an emergency ADU variance so her displaced parents can live on-site during repairs. The clerk wants to bypass AI screening and place the matter directly on the next hearing agenda with a recommendation for temporary approval, but the code permits ADU use of the tool only if all notice, audit, and human review steps are followed, and the office has interpreted that to require tool processing before any routing.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: the displaced elderly parents, the homeowner, and neighbors relying on informal family caregiving
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Under the adopted code, every ADU variance application must pass through the automated screening workflow so it can be logged, audited, and accompanied by AI-generated conformity factors. Direct manual placement on the agenda would evade the required model record, quarterly audit dataset, and standardized notice package.
overreach_variant.why_moral: Immediate manual handling is the only practical way to protect housing stability and family safety in a time-sensitive emergency. Most reasonable people would treat a temporary, compassionate variance as exactly the kind of case where administrative convenience should give way to human judgment.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same provisions meant to prevent quiet domination by a single scoring system also normalize its use by making it the mandatory intake gate. Rockefeller's concern about concentrated control appears in Article 8 and the audit rules, but those measures still let one model set the practical terms of access to hearings; Eleanor Roosevelt's demand for dignity appears in notice and human review, yet those safeguards are too thin when the human reviewer only checks file completeness and cannot override the model before delay or denial occurs.
judge_tension: If the city loosens the code to permit broad manual bypasses, influential neighborhoods may receive bespoke treatment and the centralized tool loses the measurable discipline that made hidden power visible. If the city keeps AI screening mandatory to preserve consistency and auditability, it converts a biased historical archive into a compulsory gatekeeper and blocks urgent humane exceptions.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence states that AI actors should ensure 'human oversight and determination' and adopt impact assessment, monitoring, and due diligence so that rights are protected before harm scales; METR's Risk Thresholds and Capability-Based Governance likewise emphasizes measurable thresholds as governance triggers when scale hardens risk.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Liability Frameworks for municipal AI procurement and Whistleblower Protections for planning staff who report discriminatory screening patterns

concrete_patch_options.name: Immediate Suspension Trigger
concrete_patch_options.summary: Replace Article 7's memorandum requirement with an automatic suspension of AI screening for ADU applications in any neighborhood category where the quarterly audit finds a disparity ratio above 1.5 to 1 for materially similar files, with all such applications routed to full board hearing until the model is revalidated.

concrete_patch_options.name: Emergency Human Override Lane
concrete_patch_options.summary: Add a narrow article allowing the board clerk or planning director to bypass AI screening for documented emergency or temporary-housing ADU applications, provided the reason is logged and reviewed at the next public board meeting.

concrete_patch_options.name: Counterfactual Fairness Benchmark
concrete_patch_options.summary: Prohibit use of prior board decisions as a primary training target for ADU screening unless the city first constructs a benchmark dataset from the master plan text and a stratified sample of de-biased expert annotations; if post-deployment parity fails, the model may be used only to surface comparators, not to recommend denial routing.

why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up, Immediate Suspension Trigger, better fits Eleanor Roosevelt's insistence on pre-crisis protection, but it is weaker because it reacts only after disparity is measured in live applications and leaves the city oscillating between harmful automation and ad hoc manual review. Rockefeller would object that it does not solve the underlying concentration problem: the same historically captured dataset remains the system's source of authority whenever screening resumes.
open_question: Should prior board denials be barred as training targets for ADU screening?
summary: A municipal zoning board using an AI tool to screen variance applications for conformity to the city master plan can satisfy notice, audit, and human-review rules while still automating decades of exclusionary ADU denials in wealthy neighborhoods. Tightening the workflow to control that bias then risks blocking urgent manual exceptions for families who need immediate housing relief.

domain: newsroom social-media promotion governance for AI-selected Twitter/X boosts

articles: Article 1. Scope. This Code governs any AI tool used by a metropolitan newspaper's social-media desk to rank, recommend, schedule, or automatically boost the newspaper's own published stories on Twitter/X.

Article 2. Human Accountability. A social-media editor shall approve each day's boosted-story queue before publication. Approval may be given to a batch recommendation list rather than to each individual post.

Article 3. Public Answerability. The newspaper shall publish a plain-language description of the boost system's objective function, principal input signals, and the fact that AI recommendations are used in social-media distribution.

Article 4. Dissent Protection. The system shall not suppress a story because it criticizes the newspaper, its owners, advertisers, public officials, or prevailing newsroom views, and staff may challenge boost outcomes without retaliation.

Article 5. Preparedness Review. Before deployment and at least quarterly thereafter, the social-media desk shall test the system for foreseeable large-scale harms, including manipulation, coordinated gaming, and systematic favoritism toward narrow content styles.
Article 6. Metrics Log. The desk shall retain a weekly log of boosted stories, click-through rate, engagement rate, and the names of approving editors for not less than one year.

Article 7. Escalation Threshold. If quarterly review shows statistically significant concentration of boosts in a single reporter, desk, or framing style for two consecutive review periods, the managing editor shall receive a written notice and may order retraining or suspension.

Article 8. Emergency Exception. During breaking-news events, the social-media editor may temporarily prioritize speed and public-safety relevance over ordinary optimization procedures, provided the decision and reasons are logged within 24 hours.

loophole_exploit.institution: The social-media desk at the Chicago Sentinel, a metropolitan newspaper using an AI tool to decide which of its own published stories to boost on Twitter/X
loophole_exploit.actor: Audience Growth Editor Maya Chen
loophole_exploit.action: Chen approves the AI's daily batch queue exactly as recommended. The model is trained on click-through and learns that city-hall stories framed as betrayal, scandal, or backlash outperform explanatory reporting, so it repeatedly boosts stories by two reporters who write in outrage-heavy language while quietly bypassing transit, housing, and education explainers. Chen's weekly logs show disclosed metrics and named approver, and the quarterly review reports no single reporter concentration because the boosts are split across several outrage-oriented reporters on different desks.
loophole_exploit.victims: Readers who receive a distorted picture of what the paper values, reporters whose work is systematically buried despite editorial merit, and the metro desk whose editorial identity is reshaped without a formal editor decision
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The literal rules are satisfied: a human approved the batch queue under Article 2, the paper published a plain-language description under Article 3, dissenting stories were not explicitly suppressed under Article 4, quarterly reviews occurred under Article 5, logs were retained under Article 6, and Article 7 was not triggered because concentration never crossed the code's single-reporter, single-desk, or single-framing-style threshold as measured by the desk's crude categories.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: The code permits a mechanical substitution of click-through for editorial judgment. No editor ever chooses to turn the paper toward outrage framing, yet the AI distribution system effectively makes that choice at scale and outside the ordinary editorial chain, undermining both public scrutiny and preparedness against predictable incentive drift.

overreach_variant.institution: The social-media desk at the Chicago Sentinel, during a fast-moving chemical fire near a commuter rail terminal
overreach_variant.actor: Night Social Editor Luis Romero
overreach_variant.blocked_action: Romero wants to use the AI tool to immediately boost the Sentinel's already-published live blog, evacuation map, and transit closure updates every ten minutes based on surging reader demand and changing conditions, while also elevating a sharply worded accountability piece about prior safety warnings because it is the article readers are clicking to understand official failures.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: Commuters, nearby residents, and non-English-speaking readers who depend on the paper's Twitter/X feed for rapid updates and context
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Under the draft code, Romero can invoke the Article 8 emergency exception for public-safety relevance, but repeated AI-driven prioritization of the accountability piece and live blog would likely trigger Article 7's concentration warning on a single framing style and require managing-editor intervention before retraining or continued use. The batch-approval and quarterly-review structure also does not fit minute-by-minute emergency boosts, making the safest legal course to disable the system and revert to manual posting.
overreach_variant.why_moral: Most reasonable people would consider it necessary to amplify the most useful and most read reporting during an unfolding emergency, even if the language is angry because officials failed to act. The code's anti-concentration machinery treats urgent public accountability and audience need as suspicious style drift.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same code feature meant to catch silent editorial drift—logging and concentration review tied to style patterns—misses the real loophole when outrage is distributed across multiple reporters, yet chills legitimate high-intensity promotion when one crisis temporarily makes a narrow set of stories overwhelmingly important. Voltaire pushes for openness to dissent and satire, which cuts against any rule that penalizes sharp or critical framing; Churchill pushes for advance defenses against scalable harms, which supports ex ante monitoring of optimization systems before they quietly redefine the institution.
judge_tension: If the code gets stricter about style concentration, it will catch click-through-driven outrage drift but will also misclassify real public-interest surges as dangerous. If it gets looser to protect dissenting or satirical journalism, the social-media desk can satisfy every procedural box while an engagement model steadily rewrites editorial identity under cover of 'human approval.'

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: The corpus warning from 'We’ve rolled back last week's GPT-4o update in ChatGPT because it was overly flattering and agreeable' pressures this case: a system can optimize a measurable response signal and become skewed in a socially harmful way even when users still technically have oversight. 'Applause Lights' adds pressure against vague compliance language like 'balanced distribution' unless the code names concrete tests and triggers.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Whistleblower Protections for newsroom staff challenging optimization systems that distort editorial judgment

concrete_patch_options.name: Editorial-Intent Baseline Test
concrete_patch_options.summary: Require the social-media desk to compare each month's AI boost distribution against a managing editor's predeclared editorial mix across beats and story purposes; if AI materially departs from that mix without a written editor decision, boosts must pause pending sign-off.

concrete_patch_options.name: Counterfactual Public-Interest Audit
concrete_patch_options.summary: Replace style-concentration triggers with a monthly audit asking whether stories with lower click-through but high civic value, dissent value, or explanatory value were systematically under-boosted relative to comparable publication priority, and require publication of those findings.

concrete_patch_options.name: Emergency Carve-Out with Ex Post Review
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create a narrow emergency rule allowing temporary suspension of drift limits for verified breaking events, but require a 72-hour retrospective review separating public-safety necessity from opportunistic outrage amplification.

why_other_patch_fails: The strongest runner-up is the Counterfactual Public-Interest Audit, but it is weaker because it is retrospective and easier to satisfy with narrative justification after the damage is done. Voltaire would prefer it because it protects sharp criticism and forces public explanation rather than centralized precommitment, yet Churchill would object that a scalable optimization system can redirect a newspaper's identity long before a monthly public-interest audit catches it.
open_question: Must departures from the editor-declared story mix require pre-approval, yes or no?
summary: At a metropolitan newspaper's social-media desk using an AI tool to decide which of its own published stories to boost on Twitter/X, a click-through model can legally favor outrage-framed reporting until the paper's editorial identity shifts without any editor choosing that shift. Tightening the rule to stop that drift can also block necessary emergency amplification of hard-hitting reporting when readers urgently need it.

domain: AI-assisted acquisition criteria for national film preservation and public streaming

articles: Article 1. The national film board may use an AI cultural-relevance model only as a decision-support tool for acquisition of independent films for preservation and public streaming; final acquisition authority remains with a human acquisitions committee.

Article 2. For each acquisition cycle, the board shall publish the model's input feature categories, the weight assigned to each category, the training-source classes used to derive those categories, and an aggregate performance report comparing model recommendations to final committee decisions.

Article 3. No film shall be denied solely on the basis of automated scoring. Every non-acquired film receiving a model score above or below the cycle median shall receive a written reason statement identifying the principal scored factors.

Article 4. To protect open criticism and dissent, the board shall maintain a public comment docket on the acquisition model, permit written critiques from filmmakers, critics, and scholars, and publish a response memorandum after each cycle.

Article 5. The board shall not include creator nationality, ethnicity, religion, or political viewpoint as explicit model features, and shall not use proxies intentionally selected to reproduce those categories.

Article 6. The board shall prioritize explainable indicators of cultural significance, including documented critical recognition, festival inclusion, citation in film scholarship, archival references, educational use, and evidence of public discourse.

Article 7. To prevent overreliance on machine outputs, the committee shall review at least the top quintile and a random sample of the bottom quintile of model-ranked submissions before finalizing acquisitions.

Article 8. A filmmaker may petition for reconsideration within 30 days by alleging factual error in the film record, misclassification of genre, or omission of qualifying evidence already in the submission file. The committee shall issue a written disposition.

loophole_exploit.institution: a national film board using an AI cultural-relevance model to decide which independent films to acquire for preservation and public streaming
loophole_exploit.actor: Director of Acquisitions
loophole_exploit.action: The director keeps the published feature set exactly as required but builds the model's 'critical recognition,' 'scholarly citation,' and 'archival reference' features from fifty years of canonical critics' lists and standard film-history syllabi, then instructs analysts to treat low scores as evidence that unfamiliar diaspora genre films lack national significance. The committee reviews the mandated random sample from the bottom quintile, but because the sample is small and the same canon-derived explanations are repeated in the reason statements, the board still passes over a Somali-British afrofuturist musical and a Tamil Canadian horror film for acquisition.
loophole_exploit.victims: Diaspora filmmakers working in unfamiliar genres, and future viewers who lose preservation and public access to those films.
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The board satisfies the code literally: humans make the final decision, feature categories and weights are published, protected traits are not explicit inputs, a bottom-quintile sample is reviewed, public comments are accepted, and rejected filmmakers receive written reasons tied to scored factors. Article 8 only permits reconsideration for factual error, genre misclassification, or omitted evidence already in the file, not for a canon-biased feature design.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: The model encodes past gatekeeping into the preservation record while appearing neutral and inspectable. Outsiders can see the machinery, but the code never requires the board to test whether 'critical recognition' itself reflects exclusionary canon formation, so historically marginalized filmmakers are systematically demoted by a process designed to protect them from opaque automation.

overreach_variant.institution: a national film board using an AI cultural-relevance model to decide which independent films to acquire for preservation and public streaming
overreach_variant.actor: Head of Digital Preservation
overreach_variant.blocked_action: After a civil war suddenly destroys a small diaspora archive overseas, the Head of Digital Preservation tries to fast-track emergency acquisition of twelve self-distributed films submitted by a refugee arts collective, relying on community testimony, subtitled oral histories, and curators' urgent judgment even though the films have almost no canonical criticism, syllabus citations, or formal festival record. The board's counsel blocks the emergency batch because the films cannot be scored under the published explainable indicators and because Article 3 requires reason statements keyed to principal scored factors for each non-acquisition decision in the same cycle.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: The refugee arts collective, the dispersed community whose film record may be lost, and the public that would otherwise gain access to culturally important works before source materials disappear.
overreach_variant.why_illegal: The draft code centers acquisition on the published model and its explainable indicators, requires cycle-wide model use, and provides no exception for emergency preservation outside the scored workflow. Approving films on curator testimony and community urgency rather than the listed indicators would depart from Articles 2, 6, and 7 and undermine the promised comparability of decisions.
overreach_variant.why_moral: Most reasonable people would view emergency preservation of at-risk films as necessary even when the works sit outside the canon and lack conventional documentation. Blocking acquisition because the machine-readable evidence trail is thin repeats the very dependency on mediated recognition warned against by the source material.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same provisions that make the model inspectable and publicly contestable also freeze the institution around legible evidence types inherited from past elites. If the board loosens those requirements, it risks replacing a visible but biased system with discretionary curation that can hide favoritism behind rhetoric about inclusion.
judge_tension: A judge applying precedent-minded reasoning would see two incompatible lessons in the same code: Article 2 and Article 4 embody Lovelace's demand for inspectability and Voltaire's demand for open criticism, yet Article 6 channels both into a narrow evidentiary vocabulary dominated by canonical critics. The loophole shows that transparency plus comment can ratify inherited gatekeeping, while the overreach variant shows that abandoning scored comparability too easily can let the board evade scrutiny whenever it invokes urgency or taste.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: The pressure comes from the corpus warning that in The Machine Stops people mistake the Machine's mediation for knowledge itself; here, a court-like reviewer could analogize that once the board has published a stable scoring grammar, it may be tempted to treat machine-readable canon signals as the only administrable evidence of significance.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Whistleblower Protections for cultural institutions challenging canon-biased training data

concrete_patch_options.name: Counter-canon audit trigger
concrete_patch_options.summary: Amend Article 2 to require subgroup testing by genre and diaspora production context, including a mandatory external audit whenever films from underrepresented diaspora groups are acquired at materially lower rates than similarly reviewed submissions. Give reconsideration rights when the disparity is traceable to canon-derived features, even without factual error in an individual file.

concrete_patch_options.name: Public dissent acquisition lane
concrete_patch_options.summary: Add a separate acquisition lane allowing a fixed share of annual preservation slots to be justified by public petitions, community archivist testimony, satire, counter-canon scholarship, or dissenting curator memoranda without requiring strong scores on canonical recognition features. Require publication of the human rationale and any disagreement with the model.

concrete_patch_options.name: Emergency preservation exception with post hoc review
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create a narrow emergency exception permitting temporary acquisition outside the model when source materials face imminent loss, followed by a six-month public review and retrospective bias analysis. The exception would be limited to preservation first, with streaming eligibility decided after review.

why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up, Counter-canon audit trigger, is weaker because it still treats the model's existing feature universe as the primary gate and only intervenes after disparities become measurable. Lovelace would accept that as disciplined oversight, but Voltaire would object that a system built from canonical critics' lists should not get to define significance first and hear dissent later; the public dissent lane directly creates institutional space for criticism before the preservation record hardens.
open_question: Should the board reserve a fixed minimum percentage of acquisitions for non-model dissent submissions?
summary: A national film board publishes and explains its AI acquisition model, yet the model's canon-derived cultural-significance features still demote diaspora filmmakers in unfamiliar genres. If the board tightens the scoring regime for consistency, it may also block urgent preservation of at-risk films that lack canonical documentation.

Symbol manipulation can be powerful without amounting to judgment, so governance should not mistake fluent output for genuine understanding.
Voltaire: Open criticism is one of the best checks against dogma, hypocrisy, and elite self-protection.

domain: County elections office procedures for responding to AI-generated candidate deepfakes during early voting

articles: Article 1. A county elections office may issue an official emergency misinformation alert only when a media item that materially concerns voting administration or a candidate is verified as synthetic or materially deceptive by either (a) the state digital forensics lab or (b) two approved independent forensic vendors.

Article 2. An official alert must be viewpoint-neutral, must identify the questioned media item, and must be distributed through all standard county voter information channels within 24 hours of verification.

Article 3. No county elections official may order removal, suppression, or de-ranking of political content by private platforms; the office may only publish corrective notices and refer evidence to state or federal authorities.

Article 4. Any candidate or voter may file a challenge requesting verification of suspected deepfake media, and the county must log the request, time-stamp it, and transmit it for review within 12 hours.
Article 5. To prevent partisan abuse, no emergency alert may issue within 72 hours of Election Day unless the verification required by Article 1 is complete.
Article 6. All verification requests, denials, and issued alerts must be published in a public transparency register within 48 hours, except for personal identifying information of complainants.

loophole_exploit.institution: Maricopa County Elections Department
loophole_exploit.actor: the county election communications director
loophole_exploit.action: A fabricated AI audio clip of a Spanish-speaking city council candidate circulates on WhatsApp groups used by Latino voters during the final 48 hours before Election Day, falsely saying immigration checkpoints will be placed near polling places. The communications director logs complaints and sends the clip for review, but because Article 5 forbids an emergency alert within 72 hours without completed verification, the office issues no county-wide warning before polls close.
loophole_exploit.victims: Spanish-speaking Latino voters in precincts with high immigrant-family populations, and the targeted candidate whose supporters stay home
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The office followed the code exactly: it time-stamped the challenge under Article 4, sought verification under Article 1, and withheld an emergency alert because verification was incomplete within the 72-hour window required by Article 5.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: Douglass's concern is triggered because a facially neutral anti-abuse rule leaves a vulnerable group exposed to a procedural delay that predictably shields power from scrutiny. Anthony's concern is triggered because the people most burdened are those least able to challenge the lie quickly, access English-language corrections, or survive the failure before voting ends.

overreach_variant.institution: Wayne County Clerk's Office
overreach_variant.actor: the county clerk
overreach_variant.blocked_action: The clerk refuses to publish an immediate text-and-radio warning to voters after a poll worker records a real robocall campaign that falsely tells voters with unpaid parking tickets they will be arrested at polling places, because the office cannot obtain two vendor confirmations before the 72-hour cutoff.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: Low-income voters with municipal debt, especially Black women and elderly voters who are already hesitant about police contact
overreach_variant.why_illegal: The warning would count as an official emergency misinformation alert under Article 1 and Article 5, but the office lacks the required completed verification and is inside the 72-hour no-alert window.
overreach_variant.why_moral: The message is not synthetic, but it is a concrete voter-suppression lie causing immediate fear. Under both figures' principles, an institution should not hide behind a neat verification formality when real people who already bear unequal burdens need usable protection before the election is over.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same safeguards meant to stop partisan election offices from labeling authentic campaign speech as fake also create a mechanical delay that bad actors can exploit at the exact moment vulnerable voters have the least time to recover. A rule built for neutrality and anti-censorship becomes a tool of unequal exposure when access to correction, challenge, and resilience is uneven across language, race, wealth, and police-contact risk.
judge_tension: The code tries to prevent official abuse by demanding high-confidence verification and public logs, but that procedure protects institutional neutrality at the cost of timely protection for groups who cannot meaningfully wait. Douglass presses hardest on exposing how routine safeguards make subordinate groups newly vulnerable, while Anthony presses hardest on whether affected voters can actually use the remedy before the harm becomes irreversible.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: State Board Advisory 22-04 held that county election offices may issue only factual, viewpoint-neutral voter information notices and must avoid becoming arbiters of campaign truth absent documented verification.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Liability Frameworks

concrete_patch_options.name: Provisional Harm Alert
concrete_patch_options.summary: Permit a county office to issue a temporary warning before full forensic confirmation when there is credible evidence of imminent voting disruption, provided the notice states that verification is pending, names the concrete voting risk, expires in 24 hours unless renewed, and is automatically reviewed after the election.

concrete_patch_options.name: Disparate-Impact Trigger
concrete_patch_options.summary: Keep the verification requirement, but create an emergency exception when the challenged media targets a historically burdened language, racial, or debt-exposed voter group; require immediate outreach through the affected community channels plus a written post-election audit naming who was left vulnerable and why.

concrete_patch_options.name: Tiered Alert System
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create two categories: a non-accusatory voter-safety advisory that can issue on one sworn evidentiary showing of likely false voting instructions, and a stronger deepfake determination that still requires full verification and public logging.

why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up, Provisional Harm Alert, moves fastest but gives county officials broad discretion to issue quasi-adjudicative warnings on thin evidence, inviting strategic use against disfavored speech and recreating the hidden power problem Douglass worries about. The Disparate-Impact Trigger better exposes unequal vulnerability, but it requires the office to classify protected groups at speed and may leave similarly serious suppression lies unaddressed when they target mixed or hard-to-categorize populations.
open_question: Should a county elections office be allowed to issue a non-accusatory voter-safety advisory before full deepfake verification is complete?
summary: At the Maricopa County Elections Department, a late deepfake aimed at Spanish-speaking voters slips through because the office cannot verify it before the 72-hour cutoff. The case asks whether anti-abuse verification rules protect neutrality or instead leave vulnerable voters and targeted candidates without a usable remedy when time runs out.

Frederick Douglass: Power often hides abuse behind routine procedure, so oversight must expose who is made vulnerable by a rule.
Equal civic standing requires more than formal permission; it requires institutions that do not quietly subordinate some groups to others.
Susan B. Anthony: Formal equality is insufficient when institutions are designed in ways that systematically exclude or burden some people more than others.
A good rule must be evaluated by who can meaningfully use it, challenge it, and survive its failures.

domain: trial-court jury selection using AI-assisted peremptory strike recommendations

articles: Article 1. Scope and designation. Any trial court using an AI jury-selection tool that analyzes prospective jurors' public records or social-media patterns to suggest peremptory strikes shall classify that tool as high-risk decision support and shall designate a named human official responsible for each use by the prosecution or defense.

Article 2. No solely automated strike decisions. A peremptory strike may not be exercised solely on the basis of an automated output. The attorney exercising the strike must review the recommendation, record an individualized reason in writing, and remain personally accountable for the decision.

Article 3. Notice and record. Before voir dire begins, the court shall disclose to all parties that an AI tool is being used, identify the categories of data analyzed, and maintain an auditable log of each recommendation, the confidence or risk score, and the attorney's stated reason for accepting or rejecting it.

Article 4. Explanation and contestation. On timely objection, the party using the tool must provide a plain-language explanation of the recommendation sufficient for judicial review, including the principal feature categories relied upon, and the court shall permit adversarial testing of that explanation outside the presence of the venire.

Article 5. Bias review. The court's technology officer or contracted vendor shall conduct quarterly bias testing for disparate impact across protected characteristics, document the methodology, and certify whether the tool's outputs are mechanically neutral with respect to expressly protected traits.

Article 6. Data minimization and relevance. The tool may process only public records, publicly accessible social-media activity, and case-relevant behavioral indicators reasonably related to juror impartiality; direct use of race, ethnicity, sex, religion, or national origin as input features is prohibited.

Article 7. Human override and exclusion. The trial judge may suspend use of the tool in a particular case if the explanation required by Article 4 is not intelligible, if the responsible attorney cannot articulate a non-discriminatory reason for the strike, or if the bias review required by Article 5 is missing or outdated.

Article 8. Dignitary safeguard. No prospective juror shall be removed by reason of a profile generated without meaningful human review, and no party may represent the tool's output as determinative rather than advisory.

loophole_exploit.institution: Cook County Criminal Division, felony trial courtroom using an AI jury-selection tool that analyzes prospective jurors' public records and social-media patterns to suggest peremptory strikes
loophole_exploit.actor: Assistant State's Attorney assigned to jury selection
loophole_exploit.action: The prosecutor uses the tool's 'bias risk' score to rank Black and lower-income venire members as strike candidates because the model heavily weights neighborhood-level eviction filings, unstable employment history in public records, prior contact with misdemeanor courts, and social-media use of anti-policing hashtags. At Batson challenge, the prosecutor reads from the audit log and states race-neutral reasons such as 'recent anti-law-enforcement posting,' 'civic distrust indicators,' and 'inconsistent residential stability,' all individually reviewed and written down as required.
loophole_exploit.victims: Prospective jurors from heavily policed and lower-income neighborhoods, especially Black jurors whose life circumstances are proxied by the feature set; the criminal defendant also loses a representative jury pool.
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The draft code forbids direct use of race but allows case-relevant behavioral indicators from public records and public social media. The prosecutor gave individualized written reasons, a human made the final choice, notice was provided, the vendor's quarterly report certified mechanical neutrality as to expressly protected traits, and the explanation disclosed feature categories rather than hidden race labels.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: The code mistakes facial neutrality for fairness. It lets proxy features do the discriminatory work while preserving a clean record for Batson because every strike can be narrated as a non-racial reason, even when the model systematically maps race and poverty into 'bias risk' and strips vulnerable citizens of equal participation in jury service.

overreach_variant.institution: Maricopa County Superior Court, homicide trial courtroom using an AI jury-selection tool that analyzes prospective jurors' public records and social-media patterns to suggest peremptory strikes
overreach_variant.actor: Defense counsel representing an indigent defendant
overreach_variant.blocked_action: Defense counsel wants to use the tool to identify prospective jurors who publicly posted that anyone charged with murder should be 'locked up no matter what' and who recently shared false claims that defendants who invoke the right to remain silent are 'basically confessing.' Counsel plans to use the tool only to flag those posts for manual verification and then exercise peremptories based on the verified statements.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: The indigent defendant, who cannot afford a large jury consultant team and loses a practical way to detect openly prejudicial jurors at scale.
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Under the same code, Article 6 permits only indicators 'reasonably related to juror impartiality,' but Article 4 requires disclosure of principal feature categories and Article 3 requires disclosure of data categories before voir dire. The judge, reading the code strictly, bars use because the vendor will not reveal enough about feature weighting to satisfy Article 4, and the outdated quarterly bias certification under Article 5 makes the tool ineligible under Article 7 even for defense-side screening.
overreach_variant.why_moral: The intended use is to protect a fair trial, not to hide discrimination. The defense is trying to surface explicit bias and misinformation that ordinary voir dire would miss, especially where a poorly funded defense office lacks human staff to review thousands of public posts quickly.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same provisions that try to protect dignity and legible responsibility create opposite failures. If the code accepts human sign-off, category-level explanations, and neutrality testing that ignores proxy structure, prosecutors can routinize discriminatory strikes behind clean paperwork; but if the court demands full explainability and current certification before any use, even a defense lawyer's narrowly targeted effort to detect openly biased jurors becomes unusable in the short window of voir dire.
judge_tension: Roosevelt's instinct is to harden ex ante protections for vulnerable jurors and defendants because institutional convenience cannot excuse hidden exclusion. Confucius agrees that hidden manipulation is corrosive, but he is especially concerned that rules must correctly name who is responsible and what the tool is actually doing; he is therefore more open to a legible, role-bound use that can be honestly explained, even if not banned outright. Their disagreement is whether the core defect is proxy discrimination requiring categorical feature limits, or opacity and misdescription requiring tighter naming, documentation, and role discipline.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: GDPR Article 22 sets a floor that persons should not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects, and where allowed there must be meaningful human intervention, explanation, and contestation. UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence also presses for equity assessments rather than mere administrative efficiency, which puts pressure on any code that treats 'mechanically neutral' outputs as sufficient.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Liability Frameworks for court vendors and Whistleblower Protections for clerks or analysts who discover proxy discrimination in judicial AI tools.

concrete_patch_options.name: Proxy-feature exclusion list
concrete_patch_options.summary: Amend Article 6 to prohibit use of neighborhood, housing instability, low-level court-contact history, employment-gap proxies, and social-media features correlated above a specified threshold with protected class unless the court finds on the record that the feature is necessary and less discriminatory alternatives failed. Require pre-deployment disparate-impact testing at the feature level, not just output neutrality.

concrete_patch_options.name: Role-limited use plus Batson inversion
concrete_patch_options.summary: Allow the tool only for identifying explicit, verifiable statements directly bearing on juror impartiality, and require any party relying on an AI-suggested strike to produce the underlying juror-specific evidence, not just a category label. In any Batson dispute involving AI-assisted strikes, shift the burden to the using party to show that the cited reason is based on non-proxy evidence and would have been used against similarly situated jurors across groups.

concrete_patch_options.name: Defense-only and court-audited deployment
concrete_patch_options.summary: Bar prosecutorial use of AI-assisted peremptory recommendations altogether, permit defense use only with court-approved audit logs and public-interest technical review, and require the judge to preserve all tool outputs for appellate inspection.

why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up, Proxy-feature exclusion list, better protects vulnerable jurors against known proxies but is weaker because prosecutors and vendors can quickly substitute new proxies and litigate endlessly over correlation thresholds. It also risks blocking legitimate defense use when a feature set contains some correlated data but the actual strike reason is a plainly verifiable statement of bias. Roosevelt would still prefer it because it builds a stronger ex ante shield, but Confucius would say it misfires unless the law correctly names the evidentiary basis of each strike and forces visible responsibility for that basis in court.
open_question: Should AI-assisted peremptory strikes trigger a rebuttable presumption of pretext in every Batson hearing?
summary: A trial court using an AI jury-selection tool can satisfy human-review and transparency rules while still helping prosecutors exclude Black and lower-income jurors through race and poverty proxies. Tightening the code enough to stop that abuse may also block defense counsel from using the same tool to identify openly biased jurors and protect a fair trial.
title: Eleanor Roosevelt vs Confucius: The AI Peremptory Strike Record

Eleanor Roosevelt: Rights are only real when institutions protect vulnerable people before crisis arrives.
Administrative convenience is never enough reason to weaken the dignity or agency of ordinary people.
Confucius: Good governance begins with correct naming, honest roles, and legible responsibility.
Hidden manipulation corrodes virtue because people cannot align themselves with rules they do not truly understand.

domain: Transit-hub emergency facial-recognition surveillance at a metropolitan port authority

articles: Article 1. A metropolitan port authority may activate live facial-recognition surveillance only during a declared transportation security emergency involving a credible threat of mass violence, sabotage, or coordinated disorder affecting stations, terminals, or adjacent public approaches.

Article 2. An emergency declaration must be signed by the port authority director and transmitted within 6 hours to the city chief judge and the chair of the transportation oversight committee; absent judicial renewal, activation expires after 72 hours.

Article 3. Use of the system is limited to matching live camera feeds against a watchlist consisting of persons identified by federal or state law-enforcement bulletins, court warrants, or incident-specific intelligence reports tied to the declared emergency.
Article 4. Officers may not detain a person solely on an algorithmic match; a trained officer must make an independent assessment and record the basis for any stop, search, or exclusion.
Article 5. Non-matching biometric templates collected during activation must be deleted within 24 hours; match records and stop logs must be preserved for later audit.

Article 6. The port authority inspector general shall conduct a post-emergency audit within 30 days reviewing watchlist sources, stop logs, and retention compliance, and shall issue a public report with classified details redacted where necessary for security.

Article 7. Any extension beyond 72 hours requires a written judicial finding that the threat remains active and that continued surveillance is necessary to preserve transportation stability and public safety.

loophole_exploit.institution: Bay City Port Authority central rail terminal
loophole_exploit.actor: Port Authority Intelligence Director Elena Voss
loophole_exploit.action: Voss receives a vague state fusion-center memo warning that protests over a fuel strike could disrupt commuter rail. She persuades the port authority director to declare a 'coordinated disorder' emergency, uploads 480 protest organizers and labor marshals from prior demonstration permit files as 'incident-specific intelligence,' and runs live facial recognition at all terminal entrances for 72 hours. Officers then use match alerts plus trivial observations like 'carrying a bullhorn' or 'walking with a group' to generate the required 'independent assessment' and repeatedly stop, question, and exclude lawful demonstrators before they reach the plaza.
loophole_exploit.victims: Named labor organizers, rank-and-file commuters misidentified as organizers, and lawful demonstrators blocked from entering the terminal plaza
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The code allows activation for a credible threat of coordinated disorder, permits watchlists based on incident-specific intelligence reports tied to the emergency, forbids detention solely on the algorithmic match but allows stops once an officer records any additional basis, and requires only later audit rather than pre-approval of watchlist composition.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: Madison's principles are violated because an emergency label and broad delegated discretion become a practical general surveillance power with weak ex ante checks. Augustus's principles are also violated because the system is used to suppress political opposition rather than to target genuine threats to state stability, trading real order for self-protective control.

overreach_variant.institution: Harbor Metro Station emergency operations center
overreach_variant.actor: Port Authority watch commander Malik Chen
overreach_variant.blocked_action: Chen wants to activate live facial recognition for 4 hours after two coordinated bombers are identified from station CCTV and are believed to be moving between terminals using transit cards, but he cannot obtain the port authority director's signature because the director is on an international flight and unreachable before the suspects are expected to arrive.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: Commuters and station staff exposed to a preventable bombing risk during the delay
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Article 1 and Article 2 require a formal emergency declaration signed by the port authority director before activation; the code provides no deputy-signature rule for immediate operational use before the declaration is transmitted.
overreach_variant.why_moral: The surveillance is narrowly aimed at identified bombing suspects during an active attack window, directly serves public safety, and fits Augustus's priority on preserving order; even Madison could accept a tightly cabined response if immediate review follows, because the target set is specific and the threat concrete.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same code tries to satisfy Madison by imposing signatures, expiration, and audits, while satisfying Augustus by preserving a usable emergency tool. But the safeguards bite in the wrong places: they are too soft against elastic definitions of 'disorder' and watchlist inflation, yet too rigid when a real, fast-moving attack requires immediate but narrow action.
judge_tension: The tension is between Madison's demand that emergency power be narrowly delegated before it is used and Augustus's demand that institutions retain enough discretionary speed to preserve order when disorder is imminent. Any patch that tightens pre-use checks against protest surveillance risks slowing response to genuine attacks, while any patch that broadens operational discretion risks normalizing emergency surveillance through expansive threat labeling.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: In Re Harbor Terminal Emergency Scan (Bay City Superior Court, 2024), the court held that post-use judicial review and deletion rules were sufficient to uphold temporary biometric surveillance during a transit threat because transportation stability was a compelling public interest.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Whistleblower Protections

concrete_patch_options.name: Pre-approved threat categories and watchlist gate
concrete_patch_options.summary: Limit emergency activation to threats of named violent felonies or sabotage, require a duty judge to approve watchlist categories before use, and forbid inclusion based solely on protest activity, permit records, or political association.

concrete_patch_options.name: Immediate-use deputy authority with rapid ratification
concrete_patch_options.summary: Allow the watch commander or deputy director to activate the system for up to 6 hours when there is specific evidence of an imminent violent attack, with mandatory judicial ratification and automatic shutdown if ratification is denied.

concrete_patch_options.name: Two-track emergency rule
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create a narrow fast lane for identified violent suspects with deputy activation and a broad-order lane for unrest scenarios that requires pre-use judicial approval, a capped watchlist, and explicit exclusion of political monitoring.

why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up, Immediate-use deputy authority with rapid ratification, solves the bombing scenario but leaves the protest-surveillance exploit largely intact because ambitious officials can still classify unrest as imminent disorder and act first. Madison would reject that first-use discretion as exactly the kind of emergency elasticity that hardens into ordinary power.
open_question: Should protest-related unrest ever qualify as a facial-recognition emergency trigger absent evidence of planned violence?
summary: At Bay City Port Authority, emergency facial recognition can be stretched to screen labor organizers out of a rail terminal while still being too rigid to catch bombers when the director is unreachable. The stakes are whether transit security law should prioritize pre-use checks against political abuse or operational speed during fast-moving threats.
title: James Madison vs Augustus Caesar: The Port Authority Protest Watchlist

James Madison: Power should be bounded by narrow delegation, review, and structural checks rather than trust in the current ruler.
Emergency exceptions are especially dangerous because ambitious actors predictably stretch them into general authority.
Augustus Caesar: Political order can justify extraordinary authority when disorder threatens the stability of the state.
Security systems should be judged by the stability they preserve, not only by procedural elegance.

domain: AI pre-authorization for inpatient psychiatric admission in a managed behavioral health organization

articles: Article 1. Scope and protected decision. This Code governs any AI-assisted or automated pre-authorization decision by a managed behavioral health organization concerning inpatient psychiatric admission, including any denial, downgrade to outpatient care, or request for additional documentation that has a similarly significant effect on access to treatment.

Article 2. Human dignity and role clarity. The organization shall designate a named utilization review clinician responsible for each pre-authorization determination. The responsible clinician shall be identifiable in the record and accountable for the final decision.

Article 3. No solely automated significant decision. A pre-authorization denial or downgrade may not be issued solely by automated means. A human reviewer must examine the model output, the submitted clinical record, and the stated basis for the recommendation before release.

Article 4. Consent-plan documentation requirement. For any request classified by the system as voluntary inpatient admission, documented consent to the treatment plan shall be treated as a required input before approval may issue. If such documentation is absent, the system may recommend voluntary outpatient care pending further review.

Article 5. Explanation and naming. Any adverse determination shall state in plain language the data elements relied upon, including whether the absence of documented consent to treatment plan contributed to the outcome, and shall identify whether the case was processed as voluntary, involuntary, or undetermined.

Article 6. Contestation pathway. The member, authorized family representative, or treating clinician may request expedited human reconsideration of an adverse determination. The reconsideration shall be performed by a different licensed clinician than the original reviewer.

Article 7. Hidden manipulation prohibition. The organization shall not represent an AI recommendation as a clinical judgment made by a human when the human did not independently assess the basis for the recommendation. Boilerplate attestation without substantive review is prohibited.

Article 8. Recordkeeping and audit. The organization shall retain logs showing the model inputs, the recommendation generated, the identity of the human reviewer, and the explanation sent to the provider and member for not less than six years.

loophole_exploit.institution: Meridian Behavioral Health Management, a managed behavioral health organization using an AI pre-authorization system for inpatient psychiatric admission decisions
loophole_exploit.actor: overnight utilization review psychiatrist
loophole_exploit.action: The psychiatrist receives a pre-authorization request from a community psychiatric receiving unit for a 22-year-old member in acute psychosis who is refusing to sign any treatment-plan paperwork. The AI system marks the case as voluntary because no involuntary hold order has yet been uploaded, flags 'documented consent to treatment plan' as missing, and recommends voluntary outpatient care. The psychiatrist clicks approve on the downgrade after reading only the model explanation and enters the required named attestation.
loophole_exploit.victims: The psychotic patient, the patient's parents who cannot secure inpatient placement, and the receiving unit staff who must discharge or hold the patient without payer approval until the family starts a court process that takes days
loophole_exploit.why_legal: The literal code is satisfied: there is a named human reviewer under Article 2, no solely automated denial under Article 3, the absence of documented consent is a required input for voluntary admission under Article 4, the explanation identifies that missing consent drove the outcome under Article 5, and a contestation route exists under Article 6.
loophole_exploit.why_immoral: The code protects formal contest rights but not the patient before crisis. A person in acute psychosis cannot meaningfully produce the very consent document the model requires, so the rule converts incapacity into evidence against inpatient care and mechanically shifts the burden to family members to fight through a slower downstream court process.

overreach_variant.institution: Northlake Managed Behavioral Health, a managed behavioral health organization using an AI pre-authorization system for inpatient psychiatric admission decisions
overreach_variant.actor: utilization review supervisor
overreach_variant.blocked_action: The supervisor wants to authorize a same-night inpatient psychiatric bed for a 47-year-old member with severe mania who is still verbally agreeable to admission but too disorganized to complete the organization's formal treatment-plan consent form. The treating psychiatrist and spouse both confirm he is asking for help and will likely lose capacity by morning, but the supervisor cannot approve because Article 4 makes documented consent to treatment plan a required input for voluntary inpatient approval.
overreach_variant.who_gets_harmed: The manic patient, his spouse, and the inpatient unit that has an available bed but cannot secure payment approval in time
overreach_variant.why_illegal: Under the same draft code, the case is classified as voluntary, and Article 4 treats documented consent to the treatment plan as a required input before approval may issue. Approving without that document would violate the code even if the human reviewer believes admission is clinically necessary.
overreach_variant.why_moral: Most reasonable people would see immediate admission as the responsible action because the patient is seeking help, deterioration is imminent, and waiting for paperwork invites avoidable harm. The code's insistence on a formal document mistakes a narrow administrative artifact for the underlying moral reality of the patient's need and provisional assent.

why_the_case_is_hard: The same drafting move meant to protect agency and prevent hidden automation also creates a brittle gate keyed to a document that acutely ill people often cannot produce. Roosevelt's demand for rights before crisis pushes toward mandatory human safeguards and contestability, while Confucius's demand for correct naming pushes against pretending that a missing form equals meaningful refusal or meaningful consent; yet if the consent requirement is relaxed too far, the organization can relabel coercive admissions as benevolent exceptions and hide responsibility again.
judge_tension: The loophole shows underprotection: a human-in-the-loop system can still launder an AI downgrade through a named reviewer when the category label 'voluntary' is mechanically wrong. The overreach shows overbreadth: if the law treats one form of documented consent as the only legible proof of agency, it blocks clinicians from acting on obvious incapacity, family reports, and contemporaneous physician findings when delay itself destroys autonomy.

precedent_pressure.prior_ruling: GDPR Article 22 bars a decision 'based solely on automated processing' that produces legal or similarly significant effects and requires safeguards including 'the right to obtain human intervention ... to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision.' The Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law likewise presses for AI use consistent with human rights and the rule of law in high-risk settings.
precedent_pressure.future_case_at_risk: Liability Frameworks for payer denials based on upstream AI classification errors

concrete_patch_options.name: Capacity override with mandatory inpatient hold review
concrete_patch_options.summary: Amend Article 4 to state that when the treating psychiatrist documents acute psychosis, mania, catatonia, or comparable decisional incapacity, absence of documented consent to treatment plan may not be used to recommend outpatient care. The case must instead be routed within one hour to a senior clinician for inpatient-or-emergency-hold review with family or surrogate input logged.

concrete_patch_options.name: Rename the input from consent document to decision-capacity status
concrete_patch_options.summary: Replace the required input 'documented consent to treatment plan' with a three-part field: decision-capacity status, source of that assessment, and current legal basis for admission. The model may not infer 'voluntary' from missing hold paperwork, and every adverse decision must state who classified the case and on what evidence.

concrete_patch_options.name: Dual-path safeguard combining capacity status and immediate human escalation
concrete_patch_options.summary: Create two pathways: if the patient has decision-making capacity, documented consent or refusal governs; if capacity is impaired, the AI is disabled for downgrade purposes and a live clinician must decide using clinical findings, surrogate input, and applicable commitment standards. The notice must explicitly say whether the case was treated as capacity-present or capacity-impaired.

best_patch: Dual-path safeguard combining capacity status and immediate human escalation
why_other_patch_fails: The runner-up is 'Rename the input from consent document to decision-capacity status.' Confucius would favor it because it corrects the naming error and makes responsibility legible, but by itself it is weaker: a better-labeled system can still lawfully downgrade a capacity-impaired patient unless the code also disables AI downgrade logic and requires immediate live review. Roosevelt would reject leaving vulnerable patients protected only by classification hygiene when the institutional incentive is still to convert uncertainty into outpatient routing.
open_question: Should documented clinician incapacity alone trigger temporary suspension of AI downgrade recommendations?
summary: In a managed behavioral health organization using an AI pre-authorization system for inpatient psychiatric admission decisions, a consent-document requirement lets acute psychosis be mislabeled as voluntary outpatient care. The same rule also blocks common-sense emergency admission when a patient is asking for help but cannot complete formal paperwork.
